html:
Bayinnaung was king of Burma from 1550 to 1581, of the Taungoo dynasty. He built what is often called the largest empire in the history of Southeast Asia.

He was the brother-in-law and leading general of King Tabinshwehti, who had made Pegu his capital. When Tabinshwehti was murdered in 1550 the kingdom fell apart, and Bayinnaung won it back by force. Then he kept going:

  • 1555: he took Ava and the old heartland of Upper Burma.
  • 1557: he brought the Shan States under his rule.
  • 1558: Lan Na, with its capital Chiang Mai, became his vassal.
  • 1564 and 1569: he took Ayutthaya, the capital of Siam, the second time after a long siege.
  • From 1565: he fought Lan Xang in Laos again and again.

He ruled from a rebuilt Pegu, which European visitors described as a rich and splendid city. He supported Theravada Buddhism, gave gifts to shrines as far as Sri Lanka, and tried to set common laws and weights. He died while preparing to attack Arakan.

His empire rested on his personal hold over vassal kings, and it broke up soon after his death. Siam won back its freedom in the 1580s. Burmese still count him among their three greatest kings (Burmese kingdoms).
